method.description: Deterministic in-repository identity reconciliation. The three assigned identities were tested against the bytes the adopted edition already retains by extracting the Indiana packet assets from the authority archive, mapping every page of the Section 1 petition-and-order bundle to the Coalition form code printed in its own footer, and reading each sub-document's printed title from the page itself. The result was compared against the source-acquisition queue, the adopted edition manifest and the track-source relationships.
method.extractionNote: Assets were read out of Expungement_AI_RCAP_Master_Library_Edition_1_2.zip into temporary storage outside the repository and outside every worktree. Nothing was retained, committed or materialized. The adopted archive is itself a retained repository asset, which is why this is in-repository evidence and not an acquisition.
method.tooling: poppler (pdfinfo, pdftotext -layout, per-page extraction) for page mapping and face text; pdf-lib for AcroForm and per-page annotation reads; zipfile/XML for the Form ACR docx
method.assignmentConstraintObserved: The stop condition confines this job to retained repository assets and deterministic identity mapping, with no download, no issuer contact, no legal-design change and no edition edit. Every finding is derived from retained bytes.

finding.headline: All three identities are already retained, and all three are pages of one document the adopted edition already manifests. The queue's 'no_repository_binary' is wrong on all three rows. Two recorded assumptions about these identities are also wrong on the artifact, and in opposite directions: 'CCA-XP-0120-7002 Form ACR' is not a conflation of two documents, and 'Confidential Information Form' is not CCA-XP-0120-7002.
finding.acquisitionRequiredRationale: Nothing needs to be obtained from the Coalition for Court Access or from the Office of Judicial Administration. Every page these three identities name is inside IN:CCA-SECTION1-PETITION-ORDER:PACKET:EN, which the adopted edition retains as a packet_form at a pinned digest, and the Office of Judicial Administration's own generic Form ACR is retained separately at IN:Form ACR:NOTICE:EN.
finding.whatIsActuallyWrong: Three component identities point at pages of a retained bundle as though they were unretained standalone documents, one of them under a role label the artifact contradicts and one of them under a name that belongs to a different page.

widgetVersusTerminalFieldDenominator.cause: The bundle repeats caption, cause-number and petitioner-name fields across its sub-documents under shared field names, so one terminal field drives widgets on several pages. This is the same denominator hazard already recorded for the Illinois FW-CIV family, at a much larger magnitude.
widgetVersusTerminalFieldDenominator.warning: The adopted edition's field_count of 105 is the widget count. A field map keyed on 68 terminal fields and validated against 105 widgets misaligns by 37. Both numbers are recorded so the ambiguity cannot survive.
widgetVersusTerminalFieldDenominator.rendererConsequence: A renderer must write each shared field once and let every widget render, not treat repeated widgets as separate values.

correctionsToRecordedAssumptions.recorded: The queue records sourceIdentityConfidence 'two_distinct_documents_conflated_in_one_component_identity' for acquire:IN:cca-xp-0120-7002-form-acr, and the adopted edition's note on IN:Form ACR:NOTICE:EN says the Indiana normalization 'labels one component "CCA-XP-0120-7002 Form ACR", conflating the two'.
correctionsToRecordedAssumptions.measured: Page 7 of the retained bundle is a single document that carries BOTH names on its own face: the heading 'Form ACR (Access to Court Records)' and the footer code 'CCA-XP-0120-7002', paginated by the Coalition as 'Page 1 of 1'.
correctionsToRecordedAssumptions.conclusion: The component identity string is not a conflation. It names one document by its Coalition code and by its printed title, both of which the issuer prints on the same page. The label is accurate.
correctionsToRecordedAssumptions.whatIsTrue: The separate and correct point is that the Coalition's CCA-XP-0120-7002 and the Office of Judicial Administration's generic Form ACR are two different renditions of the same notice by two different issuers. Both are retained. That is a two-renditions question, not a mislabelled-component question.
correctionsToRecordedAssumptions.confidenceBasis: The heading, the body caption, the pagination and the form code were all read off the same extracted page.
correctionsToRecordedAssumptions.consequenceIfNotCorrected: A remap worker acting on the recorded assumption would split one real Coalition document into two, and would have to invent a second identity for a page that does not exist.

correctionsToRecordedAssumptions.recorded: The queue's edition12DispositionRationale for acquire:IN:confidential-information-form opens with the bare string 'CCA-XP-0120-7002', equating the Confidential Information Form with that code.
correctionsToRecordedAssumptions.measured: CCA-XP-0120-7002 is the code printed on page 7, the Form ACR notice. The Confidential Information Form is page 8 and carries no Coalition form code at all.
correctionsToRecordedAssumptions.conclusion: They are two different pages and two different instruments. The Form ACR notice on page 7 expressly names the Confidential Information Form as a separate document in its own exclusion table: 'Name or description of document: Confidential Information Form listing Petitioner's full Social Security Number; ACR grounds for exclusion: Access to Court Records Rule 5'. A document cannot be the document it lists.
correctionsToRecordedAssumptions.confidenceBasis: The page-7 exclusion table naming the page-8 document is direct textual evidence from the issuer, not an inference from adjacency.
correctionsToRecordedAssumptions.consequenceIfNotCorrected: Collapsing the two identities would delete the confidential Social-Security-Number sheet from the packet while leaving the notice that says it was filed, and would produce a filing whose own notice refers to a document the participant was never given.

twoRenditionsOfFormACR.question: The adopted edition retains an Office of Judicial Administration Form ACR as well. Which does an expungement packet use?

coalitionRendition.groundsTable: pre-filled — 'Confidential Information Form listing Petitioner's full Social Security Number' against 'Access to Court Records Rule 5'
coalitionRendition.certificateOfService: included, with mail and Indiana E-filing System alternatives

ojaRendition.officialTitle: Form ACR — Notice of Exclusion of Confidential Information from Public Access
ojaRendition.caption: generic civil template — 'Plaintiff(s) ... vs. ... Defendant(s)'
ojaRendition.groundsTable: empty placeholders — '[List here]' and '[List specific A.C.R. grounds here.]'
ojaRendition.bracketedPlaceholders: '[filing/tender]', '[party name]', '[Insert Name]', '[list names and addresses of counsel of record]'
ojaRendition.note: It also carries a drafting note: if Rule 5(A)(1 or 3), 5(B)(1 or 2) or 5(D)(2) is the basis, the specific law or statute must also be listed.

twoRenditionsOfFormACR.verdictBasis: The OJA document is a generic civil-caption template with unfilled bracketed placeholders and a plaintiff-versus-defendant caption that does not fit an ex parte expungement petition. The Coalition rendition is the same notice already adapted to the expungement caption with the grounds pre-filled. The nine components on these tracks are expungement components.
twoRenditionsOfFormACR.doNotRetireTheOjaRendition: It is the statewide generic instrument, is separately retained, and is correctly classed supporting_process. Nothing here retires or rebinds it.
twoRenditionsOfFormACR.notDecidedHere: Whether a packet should ever emit the OJA generic rendition instead is a legal-design choice. This job records which document each identity names; it does not choose the packet's contents.

isTheCurrentRepositorySourceCorrectlyBou.explanation: The bytes are retained and adopted; the defect is entirely in the component layer. All eighteen relationships carry an officialFormId naming a page rather than the retained container, all eighteen queue rows read repositoryStatus 'no_repository_binary' for pages that are demonstrably present, one identity carries a role label the artifact contradicts, and one identity carries the wrong document's name.

queueContradiction.queueSays: repositoryStatus 'no_repository_binary' and requiredAcquisition 'Acquire the current official binary from the issuing authority and manifest it.', on all eighteen rows
queueContradiction.measured: Every page named by all three identities is inside a bundle the adopted edition manifests as packet_form at sha256 b04f2941…d041c5, and the OJA Form ACR is separately manifested at sha256 21001a12…c76c3.
queueContradiction.resolution: The queue rows are wrong on their face. 'No repository binary' and 'no standalone binary' are different statements, and the second one is what is true. The same conflation is already recorded for Hawaii and Illinois; this is its third instance and the pattern should be fixed in the queue generator rather than row by row.
queueContradiction.correctionOwner: the queue owner; the queue is not this job's to write

The bundle's pages 4, 10 and 11 are placeholders reading 'Take out this page and insert your ... pages', which is the physical join between the two assets. affectedTracksAndComponents.uniformity: All three identities bind identically across all six tracks, three components per track. The reconciliation is one-to-many and deterministic with no per-track variation.
affectedTracksAndComponents.crossRouteObservation: Four of the six tracks are conviction routes whose petitions come from the CCA-XP-0220-70xx conviction inserts, yet all four bind these three attachments out of the Section 1 non-conviction bundle. That is consistent — the appearance, the ACR notice and the confidential sheet are route-independent — but it means the conviction tracks depend on a bundle whose own title says Section 1. Recorded so a later worker does not read the dependency as an error.

implementationFamilyEffect.effectOfThisJob: Three Indiana identities move from 'no repository binary, acquire from the issuer' to located pages of a retained, adopted, digest-pinned bundle, with a measured page map, a per-page widget allocation and a corrected role label. Eighteen component bindings gain a concrete target and a digest to pin. Two recorded assumptions that would have produced wrong remaps are corrected before any remap is attempted.
implementationFamilyEffect.familyReadinessStatement: The Indiana official-PDF family remains fail-closed and this job does not move it. generation_allowed is no on every Indiana packet row, the family has no captain-projected exact sources, the separate Indiana commercial-license question is unresolved for the petition and order bundles, and no approved mapping exists. No packet becomes generatable, no renderer is assigned and no field map is built.
implementationFamilyEffect.rendererObservation: A 15-page unrotated Letter AcroForm with 68 terminal fields over 105 widgets, no XFA, no encryption and no JavaScript is an acroform_fill candidate. An observation about the artifact; the lane is not assigned here.
implementationFamilyEffect.packetAssemblyObservation: Pages 4, 10 and 11 of the container are physical placeholder sheets instructing the filer to remove them and insert pages from the separate inserts asset. Any assembly that emits the container unmodified will emit three instruction sheets to a participant. Recorded as an implementation constraint, not resolved here.

terminalDispositionDetail.why: The narrowest disposition the evidence supports. It is not unresolved_identity: every document, issuer, title, role, page location and widget allocation is established from the artifact. It is not acquisition_required: the bytes are retained and adopted, and the queue's contrary statement is demonstrably wrong. It is not a pure duplicate collapse either, because the evidence went the other way on one identity — the Confidential Information Form is a genuinely separate instrument from CCA-XP-0120-7002 and must not be collapsed into it.

redundantAcquisitionWorkRemoved.rationale: None of the three should remain an open download job. Every page is retained inside an adopted asset, and no issuer interaction can resolve a component binding held in this repository.

expectedDownstreamEffect: Three Indiana acquisition keys close without a download, and eighteen components across six tracks gain a concrete retained target with a page range and a digest to pin. Two recorded assumptions are corrected before they can drive a wrong remap: one would have split a single Coalition document in two, the other would have deleted the confidential Social-Security-Number sheet by merging it into the notice that lists it. One role label is corrected from an implied fee waiver to an appearance. Edition 1.3 gains a note correction, a role correction, a denominator disambiguation and a mapping item, and needs no new bytes. No component is rebound, no receipt is created, no binary enters version control, no renderer is assigned, no memo is edited, no edition is published, no packet becomes generatable, no runtime is enabled and no track changes promotion state.
